categories.title: Getting Started
categories.subtitle: Login, navigation & first steps
categories.overview: Welcome to the Service Nexus Agent Portal. This system helps you manage travel insurance policies efficiently. After logging in with your credentials, you will see the main dashboard with a sidebar menu on the left and the workspace on the right.

steps.title: Log In
steps.description: Enter your username and password on the login screen and click "Sign In". If your account is locked after 6 failed attempts, contact your administrator.

steps.title: Navigate the Dashboard
steps.description: Use the sidebar on the left to switch between modules. The active tab is highlighted in orange. Click any tab to open that section.

steps.title: Understand Your Role
steps.description: Your access level determines what you can see and do. Normal users create policies for their office. Admins have full system access. Query users have read-only access.

steps.title: Session & Security
steps.description: Your session expires after 60 minutes of inactivity. You will need to log in again. Always use the Logout button when you are done.

tips: Your office name and username are always shown at the bottom-left of the sidebar.
If a tab shows a beige background, it means you have unsaved data in that tab. Click the red arrow button to discard and return.
The system supports both English and Arabic for names and addresses.
Policy wording documents (PDFs) are available for download on policy creation forms.

faqs.question: What do I do if my account is locked?
faqs.answer: Contact your system administrator. They can unlock your account from the Users management section. Accounts lock after 6 consecutive failed login attempts.

faqs.question: Can I work on multiple policies at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each policy tab (Individual, Inbound, Student, Group) maintains its own data independently. You can switch between tabs without losing your progress.

faqs.question: How do I change my password?
faqs.answer: Password changes are managed by your administrator. If the system requires a password change, you will be prompted upon login.

categories.title: Individual Travel Policy
categories.subtitle: Create single-traveler policies
categories.overview: Create travel insurance policies for individual travelers. The form has two steps: personal information and policy details. The premium is calculated automatically as you fill in the details.

steps.title: Open Individual Travel
steps.description: Click "Individual Travel" in the sidebar. A two-step form will appear with a progress indicator at the top.

steps.title: Fill Personal Information (Step 1)
steps.description: Enter the traveler's name (English and optionally Arabic), phone number (exactly 10 digits), gender, passport ID, date of birth, and nationality. Fields marked with a red asterisk (*) are required.

steps.title: Fill Policy Details (Step 2)
steps.description: Click "Next" to proceed. Select the destination country, inception date, and coverage period. The expiry date calculates automatically. Choose any add-ons: Trip Cancellation ($5,000 limit), Winter Sports, or COVID-19 (up to €30,000).

steps.title: Review Premium
steps.description: The premium appears on the right side in U.S. Dollars. It updates automatically when you change the period, date of birth, destination, or toggle add-ons.

steps.title: Select Payment
steps.description: Choose a payment method (Cash or On Account). If using On Account, click the "Accounts" button to select the billing account.

steps.title: Save the Policy
steps.description: Click the green "Save Policy" button. On success, you will see a confirmation and be redirected to the policy details view.

fields.name: First Name
fields.description: Traveler's first name in English (max 15 characters)

fields.name: Destination
fields.description: Travel destination country — determines coverage zone

tips: The premium recalculates instantly when you change period, date of birth, add-ons, or destination.
Expiry date is always auto-calculated — you cannot edit it manually.
Phone numbers must be exactly 10 digits or the form will not submit.
Arabic name fields are optional but recommended for bilingual documentation.
Download the policy wording PDF from the right panel to share coverage details with your client.

faqs.question: Why is the Departure field disabled?
faqs.answer: For standard Individual plans, the departure is fixed to Palestine (PAL). For Inbound plans, the destination is fixed instead.

faqs.question: How is the premium calculated?
faqs.answer: The premium depends on: traveler's age (from date of birth), coverage period, destination zone, plan type, and any selected add-ons (COVID, Trip Cancellation, Winter Sports).

faqs.question: Can I edit a policy after saving?
faqs.answer: Saved policies in Draft status can be modified. Once a policy is paid/printed, changes require an endorsement.

faqs.question: What is an endorsement?
faqs.answer: An endorsement creates a modified copy of an existing policy with a "C" suffix appended to the reference number. The original policy remains unchanged.

categories.title: Inbound / Individual
categories.subtitle: Policies for incoming travelers
categories.overview: The Inbound plan is for travelers coming into Palestine. It uses the same two-step form as Individual Travel, but with reversed origin/destination logic — the destination is pre-set to Palestine and you select the departure country instead.

steps.title: Open Inbound/Individual
steps.description: Click "InBound/Individual" in the sidebar.

steps.title: Fill Personal Information
steps.description: Same as Individual Travel — enter traveler details, passport, phone, and nationality.

steps.title: Fill Policy Details
steps.description: The departure country is now selectable (where the traveler is coming from). Destination shows "PAL" and is locked. Select inception date, period, and add-ons.

steps.title: Save
steps.description: Review the premium and click "Save Policy".

tips: Inbound policies have separate policy wording documents — make sure to download the Inbound version.
The coverage zone is determined by the departure country for inbound plans.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Individual and Inbound?
faqs.answer: Individual is for travelers leaving Palestine. Inbound is for travelers arriving in Palestine. The origin/destination fields are swapped accordingly.

categories.title: Student Plan
categories.subtitle: Insurance for student travelers
categories.overview: The Student Plan provides specialized travel insurance for students studying abroad. It uses Plan Type 11 with student-specific coverage zones and pricing. The form follows the same two-step process as Individual Travel.

steps.title: Open Student Plan
steps.description: Click "Student Plan" in the sidebar.

steps.title: Enter Student Details
steps.description: Fill in the student's personal information just like an Individual policy.

steps.title: Configure Coverage
steps.description: Select destination, inception date, and period. Student plans may have different available periods and pricing.

steps.title: Save
steps.description: Review the premium and save the policy.

tips: Student plans use different coverage zones (Zone 11 and Zone 12) with pricing tailored for students.
The available periods may differ from standard Individual plans.
Student policy wording documents contain student-specific terms.

categories.title: Group Travel
categories.subtitle: Manage company & group policies
categories.overview: Group Travel policies cover multiple travelers under one company/organization. You first enter the company and trip details, then add individual group members. Each member can have different add-ons, and the premium is calculated for the entire group.

steps.title: Open Group Travel
steps.description: Click "Group Travel" in the sidebar.

steps.title: Enter Company Information (Step 1)
steps.description: Select the group travel type, enter the company name (English and optionally Arabic), choose destination, inception date, and period.

steps.title: Add Group Members (Step 2)
steps.description: Click "Next", then click "Add Member" to open the member form. Enter each member's name, passport, date of birth, phone, gender, and select their add-ons (Trip Cancellation, Winter Sports, COVID-19). Click "Save" to add them to the group.

steps.title: Manage Members
steps.description: The members table shows all added travelers. Use the Edit button to modify a member or the Delete button to remove them. The member count badge updates automatically.

steps.title: Review Group Premium
steps.description: The total premium for all members is displayed together. It updates when you add/remove members or change the period/destination.

steps.title: Save Group Policy
steps.description: Select the payment method and click "Save Group Policy". You must have at least one member to save.

fields.name: Destination
fields.description: Where the group is traveling to

tips: You must add at least one member before saving a group policy.
All members in a group share the same destination, inception date, and period.
Each member can have different add-ons selected independently.
The total premium is the sum of all individual member premiums.
You can edit or remove members at any time before saving.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to the number of members in a group?
faqs.answer: There is no hard limit on group size. However, larger groups may take longer to calculate premiums.

faqs.question: Can members have different travel dates?
faqs.answer: No. All members in a group share the same inception date, period, and destination. For different dates, create separate policies.

faqs.question: How do I view a group policy after saving?
faqs.answer: After saving, you are redirected to the Group Policy Details view showing all members, the company info, and the total premium breakdown.

categories.title: Policy Inquiry
categories.subtitle: Search & retrieve existing policies
categories.overview: The Inquiry section lets you search for existing policies using various filters. You can search for both Individual and Group policies. Results are displayed in a paginated table, and you can click any policy to view its full details.

steps.title: Open Inquiry
steps.description: Click "Inquiry" in the sidebar.

steps.title: Choose Search Type
steps.description: Select the "Individual" or "Group" tab at the top of the form.

steps.title: Enter Search Criteria
steps.description: Fill in any combination of filters: name, passport number, policy number, policy type, date range, or office. More criteria = more precise results.

steps.title: View Results
steps.description: Click "Find Policy" to search. Results appear in a table showing key details. The system returns up to 100 individual policies or 30 group policies per search.

steps.title: Open Policy Details
steps.description: Click the policy reference number (shown as a blue link) to view the full policy details.

tips: Policy Number gives the fastest and most accurate results.
Passport Number finds all policies associated with a specific traveler.
Combine name fields with a date range for broader searches.
Use the Office filter to narrow results to a specific branch or agency.
Results are paginated with 12 items per page — use navigation buttons to browse.
For group policies, search by Company Name or Policy Number.

faqs.question: Why are my search results limited?
faqs.answer: To maintain system performance, individual searches return a maximum of 100 results and group searches return up to 30. Use more specific criteria to narrow your results.

faqs.question: Can I see policies from other offices?
faqs.answer: It depends on your role. Normal users can only see policies from their own office. Admin and Query users can see policies from all offices.

faqs.question: What do the status badges mean?
faqs.answer: Draft means the policy is created but not yet paid. Active/Printed means the policy has been paid and finalized.

categories.title: Reports
categories.subtitle: Generate & export system reports
categories.overview: The Reports Center allows administrators to generate and download system reports in CSV format. Each report can be configured with a date range before exporting.

steps.title: Open Reports
steps.description: Click "Reports" in the sidebar.

steps.title: Select a Report
steps.description: Click on a report card to expand it. Available reports: Re-Insurance Report and Policies Report.

steps.title: Set Date Range
steps.description: Select the "From" and "To" dates for the report period.

steps.title: Generate & Download
steps.description: Click "Generate". The system processes the data and automatically downloads a CSV file to your computer.

tips: Re-Insurance Report includes policy details, coverage amounts, and reinsurance allocations.
Policies Report covers all individual and group policies with premium and client details.
Reports are downloaded as CSV files that can be opened in Excel.
Only users with Admin access can generate reports.

faqs.question: What format are reports in?
faqs.answer: All reports are exported as CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files, which can be opened in Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or any spreadsheet application.

faqs.question: Can I generate a report for a specific office?
faqs.answer: Reports cover all policies within your company group for the selected date range. Use Excel filters after downloading to narrow by office.

categories.title: Premium Calculator
categories.subtitle: Quick premium estimates
categories.overview: The Premium Calculator lets you quickly estimate insurance premiums without creating a policy. This is useful for providing quotes to clients before committing to a policy. It supports Individual, Group, and Student calculations.

steps.title: Open Calculator
steps.description: Click "Premium Calculator" in the sidebar.

steps.title: Select Calculation Type
steps.description: Choose from three tabs: Individual Travel, Group Travel, or Student Plan.

steps.title: Enter Parameters
steps.description: For Individual/Student: select destination, period, and date of birth. For Group: select destination and period, then add members with their dates of birth and add-ons.

steps.title: Toggle Add-ons
steps.description: Check or uncheck COVID-19, Trip Cancellation, and Winter Sports to see how they affect the premium.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.description: Click "Calculate Premium". The result is displayed instantly in U.S. Dollars.

tips: The calculator does not save any data — it is purely for estimates.
Use it to compare prices across Individual, Group, and Student plans for the same trip.
Group premiums show the total for all members and the member count.
Add-ons can significantly affect the premium — toggle them to show clients the difference.

faqs.question: Is the calculated premium binding?
faqs.answer: No. The calculator provides estimates only. The final premium is determined when you create the actual policy and may vary if pricing has been updated.

faqs.question: Can I save or print the calculation?
faqs.answer: The calculator does not have a save or print function. Note down the result or take a screenshot to share with your client.

categories.title: Administrator Panel
categories.subtitle: System configuration & management
categories.overview: The Administrator panel provides access to system configuration and management functions. Only users with Admin role can access these features. The panel displays cards for each function — click a card to open that management section.

steps.title: Users Management
steps.description: Create, edit, delete, and lock/unlock user accounts. Assign roles (Normal, Admin, Query, Company Admin, Agencies Query), offices, and permissions.

steps.title: Currency Rates
steps.description: Manage USD to NIS exchange rates. Add new rates with effective dates. View rate history and delete outdated entries.

steps.title: Travel Agencies
steps.description: Add, edit, and delete travel agency/broker partners. View and manage agency offices.

steps.title: Company Offices
steps.description: Manage office locations and branches. Set broker codes and special discount percentages.

steps.title: Accounts
steps.description: Manage financial/cash accounts. Set credit limits, broker commission percentages, and registration IDs.

steps.title: Agency Commissions
steps.description: Configure commission rates per agency/broker. Set IRS IDs and company group assignments.

steps.title: Travel Prices
steps.description: Manage the full pricing matrix: plan type, coverage zone, period, age bracket, premium, commission, retention, re-insurance, and fees. Use filters to find specific pricing entries.

steps.title: Export Travel Data
steps.description: Export travel data and active insured client lists. Downloads are in CSV format.

steps.title: Delete Draft Policies
steps.description: Bulk-delete draft policies older than yesterday. Requires confirmation before execution.

tips: Only Admin users can access this section. If you do not see the Administrator tab, your account does not have admin privileges.
Changes to pricing take effect for new policies immediately.
Always confirm before deleting users, offices, or accounts — deletions cannot be undone.
Use the search bar in each management section to quickly find entries.
Lock a user account to temporarily disable their access without deleting the account.

faqs.question: How do user roles differ?
faqs.answer: Normal User: creates and views own-office policies. Admin: full access to everything. Query User: read-only across all offices. Company Admin: manages policies across multiple offices. Agencies Query: read-only across agency/broker policies.

faqs.question: How does the pricing matrix work?
faqs.answer: Each price entry defines a premium for a specific combination of: plan type, coverage zone, duration, and age bracket. When a policy is created, the system finds the matching price entry to calculate the premium.

faqs.question: What happens when I delete a draft policy?
faqs.answer: Draft policies that have not been paid are permanently removed. This cannot be undone. The "Delete Draft Policies" function only removes drafts older than yesterday.
